steps.title: Indefinite pronouns
steps.html:
peoplethingsplaces
some– (+)somebody / someonesomethingsomewhere
any– (? –)anybody / anyoneanythinganywhere
every–everybody / everyoneeverythingeverywhere
no–nobody / no onenothingnowhere

Use some– in positive sentences and in offers: I need something to eat. Would you like something to drink?

Use any– in questions and negatives: Is there anywhere to leave our luggage? I haven’t seen anything like this.

No– words are already negative, so the verb stays positive: Nobody’s serving food. Never say nobody isn’t serving.

They all take a singular verb: Everyone leaves their shoes outside. Nothing is open. An adjective comes after the word: somewhere cheap, not cheap somewhere.

You will use somewhere and anything again in the next lesson, at a hotel reception.
